classification.difficultyReason: Transfer equal base angles between the two isosceles triangles using an exterior angle, then relate the resulting doubled angle to beta on a straight line.

content.prompt: In the diagram below, find a formula for $\alpha$ in terms of $\beta$.

spec.description: Divided outer triangle with the left sloping side extended beyond its apex and the base extended rightwards; identical ticks on the left base segment, internal segment and right sloping side.
spec.mathematics: Left base interior angle alpha; right base exterior angle beta; two linked isosceles triangles.

answer.worked:
In the left isosceles triangle, the apex angle equals $\alpha$. Its exterior angle at the interior base point is $2\alpha$, by the exterior angle theorem. This is a base angle of the right isosceles triangle, so the right base interior angle is also $2\alpha$. It forms a straight angle with $\beta$.
$$\begin{align*}2\alpha+\beta&=180^\circ\\2\alpha&=180^\circ-\beta\\\alpha&=\frac{180^\circ-\beta}{2}.\end{align*}$$
